title: Operator-to-Customer Quick Clarity Kit — short status + action cards
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact customer-facing draft for the ongoing inference-quality incident (INC-2026-1972). Designed for rapid publication to the status page and targeted customers (enterprises with pinned models). Focus: clear signal (what happened), tangible action lanes for customers, verification options, and next-step timelines. Keep it short; include links to evidence bundle for self-audit.

Executive status (short):
- Impact window: Sep 12 03:10 — Sep 12 06:45 UTC (partial degradation persisted intermittently).
- Observed effect: elevated rate of stale or truncated structured outputs and occasionally duplicated tokens on streaming responses for ~4% of requests to model-family: redwood/fast-alpha.* (hosted API).
- Customer-visible: slow or partial responses, occasional stream reconnects, and in a small number of cases, responses missing expected structured fields.
- Current status: mitigations active, traffic routed to compatible model variant, monitoring shows steady decline in error rate. We are in rollback-validation stage.

What we did (concise timeline):
- 03:10 UTC — Detection: automated regression alert (rank stability + structured output mismatch) and customer reports from three tenants.
- 03:18 UTC — Triage: SRE + Serving Runtime oncall initiated incident channel. Initial hypothesis: KV cache eviction interplay with new kernel path on recent model-hosting release.
- 03:45 UTC — Containment: Activated model-fallback policy for affected customers (automated routing to redwood/fast-alpha-stable-quant variant), temporarily disabled the newest kernel selector in the staging partition.
- 04:30 UTC — Mitigation: We rolled traffic for 100% of affected host pools to stable variant; observed drop in error telemetry across regions.
- 05:10 UTC — Verification: Began systematic replay and evidence collection for impacted tenant request traces.
- 06:00 UTC — Candidate fix: Reverted the kernel-selection change in the serving runtime on the primary host pool.
- 06:45 UTC — Status: System telemetry within normal bounds for 60+ minutes. We transitioned to monitoring and evidence-gathering.

Customer impact: who saw what
- Tier affected: Small fraction of hosted API customers using model-family redwood/fast-alpha with streaming + structured-output flags enabled.
- Typical symptoms: partial outputs, missing JSON keys in structured responses, truncated streams, occasional duplication of trailing tokens.
- Estimated exposure: approximately 3–6% of requests in the impacted host pools during the window; fewer than 0.5% of customers experienced persistent data integrity concerns.

Action lanes for customers (choose one based on risk tolerance):
1) Immediate opt-in rollback (recommended for high-integrity workloads):
   - What we do: Pin your tenant to redwood/fast-alpha-stable-quant for 7 days (no runtime kernel selection) and run a short verification suite.
   - How to request: Reply to this message or open Jira CS-4827 and include tenant id(s). We will prioritize targeted pinning and provide an evidence snapshot.
   - Pros: lowest risk, immediate reduction in exposure.
   - Cons: slight latency uptick (~5–10% tail) for some requests.

2) Evidence-led replay and partial reconciliation (recommended for analytical customers):
   - What we do: Provide per-request trace bundles (signed timestamps + hashes) for the impacted window so you can run local replays against pinned model variants or your private deployment.
   - How to request: Use the status page evidence request form (link below) or contact your CSM.
   - Pros: full visibility, enables customer-driven verification and auditing.
   - Cons: requires engineering effort on your side for replay.

3) Self-service verification steps (for teams who prefer to act independently):
   - Quick checks: Compare response schema keys for a sample of requests; run token-delta checks on streaming sessions; inspect end-to-end timestamps for reordering signs.
   - Tools: We’ll provide a mini-toolkit script (Python) in the evidence bundle to compute schema diffs and token-hash comparisons.

Evidence and verification package (what we’ll provide):
- Signed evidence bundle: per-request trace (obfuscated PII), worker-id, kernel-selector logs, KV-cache eviction logs, and request/response hashes for the impacted window.
- Minimal replay harness: Dockerized harness + instructions to replay traces against redwood/fast-alpha-stable-quant locally or in your private deployment.
- Verification checklist: Quick commands to validate schema consistency and token-order integrity.

Customer communications we will publish (next 24 hours):
- Short status page update (public): signal + containment + ETA for post-incident customer summary.
- Targeted tenant emails: evidence bundle + action lanes for customers we detect were likely impacted (tenant-specific).
- Post-incident customer summary (within 72 hours): root cause, remediation, QA changes, and recommended model pinning guidance.

Compensation and SLA:
- If you were materially impacted (verified data loss, truncated inference), we will proactively reach out with options for service credits and/or support-led replay. Please ensure your account team has permission to accept credits.

Contact and escalation paths:
- Primary: your CSM (if assigned) — we will open a dedicated thread and attach your evidence bundle.
- Engineering/Dev contact (for customers with technical escalations): SRE oncall and Solutions Eng (contact via CS-4827).
- Urgent enterprise escalation: if you need immediate tenant pinning, reply to this doc thread or DM the incident lead in Slack #incident-1972.

Internal notes for customer-success and SEs (for awareness, keep internal reference):
- We should not speculate on root cause in public updates; keep language focused on observed signals, containment actions, and available verification.
- Prepare tailored evidence packages for high-usage tenants first (list to be assembled by solutions-eng).
- Ask legal/props for any customer-requested replay that includes PII — follow data-sharing checklist.

Draft status page update (one-line + concise bullet):
- Title: Partial degradation for redwood/fast-alpha (resolved; evidence available)
- Body: Between Sep 12 03:10 and Sep 12 06:45 UTC a subset of requests to the redwood/fast-alpha model family experienced intermittent structured-output and streaming anomalies. We routed traffic to a stable variant and reverted a kernel-selection change; monitoring indicates the issue is resolved. Impacted customers have been contacted with an evidence bundle and replay options.

Template tenant message (short - to be personalized):
Hi <CustomerName>,
We detected intermittent structured-output/streaming anomalies affecting a small subset of requests to redwood/fast-alpha on Sep 12 (03:10–06:45 UTC). We have contained the issue and begun targeted evidence collection for affected tenants. If you’d like us to pin your tenant to the stable variant or receive the replay bundle, reply to this message and include your tenant id. We can prioritize verification and support-led replay.
Thanks,
Maya (oncall CS)

Open questions (internal to resolve in postmortem):
- Exact kernel-selector condition that triggered the KV-cache eviction pattern — requires serving-runtime trace correlation.
- Why only a subset of host pools exposed the anomaly — investigate hardware/kernel scheduling differences.
- Did any customer-side SDK or streaming client patterns exacerbate symptom visibility?

Next steps (owner assignments):
- Evidence package assembly: Samir Gupta (by Sep 13 12:00 UTC).
- Tenant prioritization list for targeted pinning: Solutions Eng (Ethan Patel) by Sep 13 09:00 UTC.
- Post-incident customer summary draft (72-hour): Maya Chen + Lena Ortiz.

Attachments/links (internal):
- Incident runbook snapshot: Confluence:CI-Runbook-INC-2026-1972
- Telemetry dashboards: internal (link in incident channel)

Notes to self: keep public message short and non-technical; give customers concrete choices. For enterprise SLAs, prioritize fast tenant pinning and evidence-first workflows.

---
Editorial: this is intentionally brief and modular — publish the status page short form immediately, push the tenant emails in waves prioritized by usage, and ensure evidence bundles attach checksums and a replay harness for reproducibility.
